nodes.question: What aspect of Marine Protected Areas in Madeira has been poorly studied?
nodes.answer: The overall vulnerability of the MPAs in Madeira is still poorly studied.
nodes.paragraph: Currently, the Madeira Archipelago holds nine Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) with different pro- tection attributes and features, including one of the largest implemented no-take MPA in Europe (Alves et al. 2022) (See Study Area in Material in Methods for more details). Establishing this extensive, exclu- sively no-take MPA was a step forward in the com- mitment to assuring the EU Biodiversity Strategy and ensured the full protection of over 25% of Madeira territorial waters. There are several threats that MPAs are subjected to, including overexploitation (i.e., fishing, includ- ing illegal fishing), pollution, climate change, tour - ism (i.e., scuba diving), bioinvasions (i.e., the intro- duction of NIS) (de Oliveira J nior et al. 2020). However, the vulnerability of MPAs in Madeira is still poorly studied, with most of the work focus- ing on intertidal harvesting (e.g., Sousa et al. 2019; 2020a, b), protection effects (e.g., Ribeiro 2008; Almada 2017) or specific endangered species such as the monk seal, Monachus monachus (e.g., Pires et al.

nodes.question: What are some threats faced by Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in Madeira?
nodes.answer: Threats include overexploitation (such as illegal fishing), pollution, climate change, tourism (like scuba diving), and bioinvasions (introduction of non-indigenous species).

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What percentage of national maritime space must EU member states classify as marine protected areas by 2030?
nodes.answer: EU member states must classify 30% of their national maritime space as marine protected areas (MPAs) by 2030.
nodes.paragraph: 2022). One of the actions of such a plan was to establish a more extensive EU-wide network of protected areas on land and at sea. In the marine realm, EU member states must classify 30% of their national maritime space as marine protected areas (MPAs) by 2030. From a conservation point of Refining management strategies in marine protected areas in oceanic islands: a non indigenous 89 Vol. : (123456789) view, MPAs have been considered a practical instru- ment, namely by promoting the increase in biomass, density, abundance, species richness, and specimens size (e.g., Garc a-Rubies and Zabala 1990; Roberts 1995; Rius 2007). The designation of MPAs has been proposed as a management tool to effectively contrib- ute to the sustainable exploitation of marine resources (e.g., Plan Development Team 1990; Allison et al. 1998; Pauly et al. 2002). Madeira region has been pioneering the creation and implementation of MPAs since the Selvagens Islands Nature Reserve in 1971 (Friedlander et al. 2017). Over the following 50 years, several other protected areas were established in the Madeira Archipelago, many of which had permanent surveil- lance.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Ocean governance|Marine protected areas_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What did a previous experimental study in Madeira find regarding local MPA communities and NIS colonization?
nodes.answer: It found that local MPA communities showed lower NIS colonization than communities outside protected areas.
nodes.paragraph: 2007; 2008; Karamanlidis et al. 2016; Mclvor et al. 2023). A previous experimental study in Madeira supported that local MPA communities showed lower NIS colonisation than communities outside protected areas (Gestoso et al. 2017), sug- gesting some degree of enhanced biotic resistance against NIS invasion (Elton 1958). However, the extent of the effects or how they relate to differ - ential NIS pressure is unclear. Recent works have also focused on local NIS proliferation and possible trophic control mechanisms (Chebaane et al. 2023, 2024). However, these studies detected spatial vari- ation in trophic interactions and biotic resistance that may be related to differential NIS pressure, pro- tection status or other factors. Another recent study conducted in Madeira used statistical modelling to verify the risk of NIS spread via diving boats using environmental and survey data (Parretti et al. 2020). Model validation showed a strong correlation between predicted risks and actual NIS presence at diving sites. Results indicate higher NIS risks in MPAs, supported by increased maritime traffic related to dive operations, highlighting the need for management actions.
